Public-domain example: Pride and Prejudice

Development checkout, base version 0.9.3. The dashboard shows the first 3 chapters of Pride and Prejudice (Jane Austen); the complete work is available as a PDF analysis report.

The opening chapters are reproduced from a public-domain Project Gutenberg edition. The report uses the real chapter, paragraph and style interactions of the renderer, without server functions; it accepts no uploads and saves no edits.

Short excerpts and language-dependent heuristics support human review. This example is not a benchmark, a calibration corpus or a literary quality verdict.

Style reference

How it’s measured

The reference band is this manuscript's median ± 2 robust standard deviations, not an external target or a confidence interval. Counts show deviation-threshold hits, not FDR decisions. Select a feature to inspect its chapters.

Exploratory selection: the normal model and FDR do not provide calibrated error rates here.

Understanding the thresholds
  • Band: median ± 2.00σ; describes spread without chapter SE.
  • Deviation: |z*| ≥ 2.50, including chapter SE. The comparison share counts measurable cells below this cutoff, not inside the band.
  • BH selection: q = 0.05 on normal tails from the same chapter reference. Error-rate control has not been established.
  • Paragraph layer: |z| ≥ 1.50 after rounding to two decimals; its own reference within each chapter, separate from chapter flags.

Method, coverage and exact loadings

Each point is a chapter. Nearness applies to the displayed axes. The line follows chapter order, including gaps. Rotate or, where available, choose 2D to inspect overlaps.

The mark considers every measured axis. In 2D a hidden axis can trigger it. Use the cutoff to choose chapters to reread. FDR selection follows a separate rule.

Drag or use the rotation buttons to turn. Use Shift and the mouse wheel or the zoom buttons to zoom. Swiping vertically on touchscreens scrolls the page. Select a point to see its chapter scores.

PCA combines standardized low-to-high feature ranks within the complete chapters. The origin is their mean rank position; scores are component coordinates, not z scores.

Axes depend on this manuscript and its measured chapters. Similarity is limited to these features and displayed dimensions. Variation does not measure literary importance or quality; a cutoff does not prescribe an edit.
